page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-22-standardlssd is a memory-optimized and storage-heavy virtual machine instance. It features 22 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 11 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 176 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 6442 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity across two drives, while there are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data positions this instance in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 11688.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 27968.71. Memory bandwidth reaches 1495.22 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 99.03 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong performance in LLM text generation for small models, delivering 321.65 tokens per second, which places it in the top 25% tier. However, text generation for larger 7B models drops to an average 16.29 tokens per second.

The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for deep learning and matrix operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography. With its combination of high memory capacity, fast local NVMe SSD storage, and solid database performance, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, software compilation, and localized data processing workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-22-standardlssd is an x86_64 server instance designed for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz, it provides 22 dedicated vCPUs across 11 physical cores, paired with 176 GB of system memory and 6442 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. In performance tests, the instance delivers average multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth results, but shows strong capability in small-model LLM text generation at 321.65 tokens per second. With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage, this instance is optimized for database operations, Redis caching, software compilation, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
